basis: The receiver's investigation and the banks' replies to the receiver's letters; a manager's statement
record: A view over recorded links between accounts, where a shared attribute is recorded
bearing: Does not settle it. The receiver wrote to 45 financial institutions; 34 are marked paid, no funds, accounts closed or over drawn, and the receiver believes some frozen accounts may have been personal. The report ties the number of institutions to banks rejecting applications or closing accounts, 'at least in part', and not to a threshold. The sheet says several accounts alone are not T1. A manager said the online pharmacies 'may have used multiple processors'; that wording could mean the tactic and does not say so. The count marks T1 as not alleged in this complaint

basis: Two managers' walk-through of the business; the receiver's count of trade-name filings; for the false statements, the receiver's own belief 'based upon information I have obtained to date'
held_by: Processor. The trade names were filed with the state and the county
processor_knew: It did this itself. It filed a trade name for each merchant and deposited that merchant's payment orders in a processing account in its own name under the trade name. A manager first said the bank required the trade name and later that the bank 'really did not care'
record: The same view; with no recorded shared attribute nothing exposes it (a stated limit)
bearing: Against, for the processor: it was the actor, so no record of its own was the gap. For a bank: the account holder was one of the two companies under a trade name, and the receiver believes the accounts were opened by giving the bank false or misleading information about the type of business. The report does not say what any bank was told or checked. Trade names on file: at least 35 and at least 14 with the state for the two companies, and about 23 with the county

basis: A manager's statements; the receiver's review of trade-name filings and of the banks' replies
held_by: Processor. The trade-name filings are public
bearing: Against, for the processor: it made each change. Three changes over time. It first did business with one telemarketer, then 'switched' to a second name that the receiver was told is the same company, and 'allegedly terminated the direct relationship' with the first. One trade name was abandoned under one company on 17 October 2018 and filed under the other on 17 April 2019; the second company was registered on 12 September 2018. And as banks rejected applications or closed accounts, a manager 'went from one bank to the next', which the report gives as the reason many accounts 'were opened and closed rather quickly'. The report does not say any change was made so that history would not follow a merchant. For a bank, a successor link would have to run across banks, and no one bank's records do
locator: R 13 para 1; R 10 note 2; R 4 para 2; R 14 para 1

tactic: T7 Known and not acted on
basis: Managers' statements; the receiver's own comments
processor_knew: Its managers knew that the merchants took no card or ACH payments, and one said this was because those 'are too strictly regulated'. The processor got notices of returned payments. Banks were rejecting its applications and closing its accounts. It was processing on the day the receiver took control
bearing: Against, as far as it goes. The managers had this and kept processing; the receiver writes that the merchants' refusal of cards and ACH 'should have given Receivership Defendants concern'. Unclear because the sheet asks for return or report levels, notices, complaints or warnings about a seller, and the report gives none: no return rate, no complaint and, beyond one account blocked for an extended overdraft, no reason for a bank's refusal or closure. The count marks T7 as alleged in this complaint, which gives return rates; the report does not repeat them
locator: R 9 para 2 and note 1; R 12 item 12; R 14 para 1; R 20 to R 21

basis: Two managers' walk-through; the banks' replies
held_by: Processor; the banks, for their own accounts
processor_knew: On notice that a payment 'was NSF or returned for some reason, the amount was charged against the settlement with the Merchant', and NSF fees came out of the merchant's share. So a return it was told of was set against a merchant
bearing: Open. The protocol note fixed that tracked returns by merchant with continued processing would count against the records. The report shows returns charged to each merchant and continued processing. It states no return rate by merchant or by account and does not say the processor computed one. Three accounts at two banks were left with negative balances 'as a result of checks being returned'. The receiver later could not open the companies' programs, so the report is not written from their processing records
